changes.new: Numbered list of what must be true when the work is done. One condition per number: when a requirement joins two conditions ("X and Y"), split it into two numbers, so each one maps to an acceptance criterion.

system.recommendation: Install the agent-browser CLI on the factory machine. Have 'factory/bin/target check' (or /factory health) report when it is missing, because reviewer-ux and reviewer-ui depend on it. In job 003 both the builder and reviewer-ux found it missing ('command not found: agent-browser').

Every agent scored 70 or less on 'reply' (reviewer-ux 30). The harness tells subagents to put a full report in SubagentHandback, which conflicts with each prompt's 'reply with one line'. A person should decide which wins (for example, a sentence in skill:factory's Spawning agents section saying the handback message is that one line), rather than patching seven prompts one by one.

Grader review by a person (the retrospective may not touch factory/bin/eval). Several low scores in job 003 come from the rules, not from the work. paths_verified ignores paths seen in tool output ('git ls-files'). grounding expects AGENTS.md even when the target has none (djset has no AGENTS.md; notes.md is canonical). The OBSERVABLE regex for behavioural_criteria misses 'appears', 'is static', 'has no' and computed-value checks. evidence_per_criterion misses evidence written as sub-bullets (builder AC 4, 7 and 8 have detailed evidence but score as missing). uses_the_page scored 100 for a review the agent itself called 'code review only'.

reviewer-ux first started serve.py on the default port 8766 and then ran 'kill $(lsof -tiTCP:8766 -sTCP:LISTEN)'. That can kill another job's server. Consider adding the server's port flag or env var (HORIZON_PORT for djset) to notes:djset, so reviewers start on their own port the first time.
